title: Suggestion: highlight the importance of correct path to pdflatex in the documentation
body:
First, thank you very much for MaTeX, I'm a happy user and I love it.

Recently, MaTeX started throwing errors being unable to locate `lmodern.sty`.  The reason was in an incorrectly set up path to `pdflatex`, and I quickly fixed it.

In more detail, now I have two installations of TeXLive on my Linux system.  One is a full native install, and the second one is a small installation from arch repositories.  I needed this second one because some other packages marked `texlive` as a mandatory dependence.  As a result, in a shell, `which pdflatex` points to my native installation which has `lmodern.sty`.  In Mathematica, it points to the packaged installation which doesn't have this package.

Of course, there are multiple ways to fix it, but it took me some time to figure out the reason, and I believe this exact situation deserves to be mentioned in the documentation.

title: Suggestion: add instruction in documentation for supporting Chinese
body:
* Use xelatex executable binary instead of the default pdflatex: `ConfigureMaTeX["pdfLaTeX" -> "/Library/TeX/texbin/xelatex"]`
* Include support to Chinese text in the preamble via the option to MaTeX: `SetOptions[MaTeX, "Preamble" -> {"\\usepackage[UTF8]{ctex}"}]`
* Verify: `MaTeX["\\text{之乎者也} \\sum_{k=1}^{\\infty} \\frac{1}{k}"]`

title: Tick labels have weird minus signs
body:
**Describe the bug**

Trying out the first Usage Example in [the blog post](http://szhorvat.net/pelican/latex-typesetting-in-mathematica.html) results in tick labels with weird minus signs. As far as I know, I have properly installed all necessary fonts (whole `Latin Modern` family).

Using `MaTeX` to generate all tick labels is a possible workaround, but isn't very convenient. Do you have any idea how to nudge `Mathematica` to properly use `Latin Modern` font in the tick labels?

**To Reproduce**

<!-- Below, show the sequence of commands to reproduce the issue in a fresh Mathematica kernel. Be sure to use the latest version of MaTeX. -->

```mma
Needs["MaTeX`"]
texStyle = {FontFamily -> "Latin Modern Roman", FontSize -> 12};
contour = 
 ContourPlot[x^2 + y^4 == 1, {x, -1.2, 1.2}, {y, -1.2, 1.2}, 
  BaseStyle -> texStyle, 
  Epilog -> {Arrow[{{0.1, 0.3}, {0.5, 0.80}}], 
    Inset[MaTeX["x^2+y^4=1", Magnification -> 2], {0.1, 0.3}, 
     Scaled[{0.5, 1}]]}]
```

**Additional information**

 - MaTeX version: 1.7.10
 - Mathematica version: 14.1

title: Build a PacletSite in this github repository
body:
With this improvement, users can simply write `PacletInstall["MaTeX"]` to fetch the newest and compatible version of MaTeX after executing `PacletSiteRegister@"https://github.com/szhorvat/MaTeX/raw/master"`.

Put all paclets in the `/Paclets/` directory, and export the `PacletSite[Paclet[Name->..., ...], ...]` expression as ZIP to `/PacletSite.mz`, then everything will be OK.

You can use the `PutSiteInfo[]` function to conveniently create `PacletSite.mz` in this paclet:
`PacletInstall["WolframPacletSiteManager", "Site"->"https://github.com/rnotlnglgq/WolframPacletSiteManager/raw/master"]` .

https://mathematica.stackexchange.com/questions/218254/how-to-set-up-own-paclet-server/243689

It has now happened multiple times that people assumed that they need to provide the path to the directory containing Ghostscript rather than the Ghostscript executable.  Example: #23

title: Use another engine instead of LaTeX to improve performance
body: @szhorvat Thank you for the development of MaTeX. I found that MaTeX is slow since the conversion process is complicated. If we only need to render math symbols or equations, there are other rendering engines(libraries) that is fast and can be integrated smoothly into Mathematica. I searched the Internet and found the Java library [jlatexmath](https://github.com/opencollab/jlatexmath) that can do the job. And I tried an application [mathematicallatexhelper](https://github.com/moritzfl/mathematicallatexhelper) that uses this library and found it very fast. I know the [J/Link](http://reference.wolfram.com/language/JLink/tutorial/CallingJavaFromTheWolframLanguage.html#19690) can be used to integrate this library into Mathematica, and I wonder if this is a good solution.

title: compatibility with ghostscript 9.21
body:
Hi there, I have problems running MaTeX against ghostscript release 9.21 on Arch linux. It seems MaTeX does not recognize the binary as a valid ghostscript:

`/usr/bin/gs is either not working or is not Ghostscript.`
`Please configure Ghostscript using ConfigureMaTeX["Ghostscript" -> "path to gs executable..."]`

Quick fix:
Build ghostscript-9.20 from source and run
`ConfigureMaTeX["Ghostscript" -> "/path/to/gs-9.20/bin/gs"]`

If you need any more information, please let me know.

title: Investigate using true display mode
body:
As of version 1.7, MaTeX only supports inline math. It achieves the display style look using `\displaystyle`.

There are certain commands that only work in display mode, such as `\begin{multline}` or `\begin{split}`. Unfortunately cropping tightly and not setting a page width with the `standalone` package is problematic.

TODO: Investigate if there are any good solutions for allowing true display mode.  What compromises will be necessary?

title: MaTeX should work with StringForm
body:
This is not an issue but a feature request and this might be just a matter of taste. 

I recently found that MaTeX cannot handle StringForm correctly, e.g.,

```
StringForm[ "\\frac{x}{``}", 3] // MaTeX
```

gives an unexpected result. I know there is a very simple workaround such as

```
StringForm[ "\\frac{x}{``}", 3] // ToString // MaTeX
```

I understand that MaTeX should not have all possible overloads for arbitrary heads. However, I think StringForm is primitive enough to be considered special.

title: Check whether the pdflatex exists.
body:
I tested your package today and found it was very helpful. After configuration, however, I had to spend some time since I could not get correct results. It turned out that I only configured the directories where the pdflatex lives but did not specify pdflatex (i.e., /some/other/directory/ not /some/other/directory/pdflatex).  However, it did not warn me but yielded errors few lines after when it tried to run ghostscript(that is why I initially doubted that my ghostscript configuration was wrong). It would be nice if you add some codes that check whether pdflatex is correctly configured.  IMO, DirectoryQ[ path]` is sufficient for this check.  

By the way, thank you for your nice package. I really like it.
